message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run** example that creates a new Compute Engine VM on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) with:

| Requirement | How it’s satisfied |
|-------------|--------------------|
| **GPU** – NVIDIA RTX A6000 | `--accelerator type=nvidia-a6000,count=1` |
| **OS** – Ubuntu 20.04 LTS | `--image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud` |
| **Machine type** – balanced CPU & memory | `n1-standard-8` (8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM) |
| **Boot disk size** – 50 GB | `--boot-disk-size=50GB` |
| **Zone** – pick one that supports GPUs (e.g., `us-central1-b`) | `--zone=us-central1-b` |

---

## 1️⃣ gcloud CLI Command

```bash
gcloud compute instances create my-rtx-a6000 \
    --zone=us-central1-b \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=50GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-balanced \
    --accelerator type=nvidia-a6000,count=1 \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --restart-on-failure \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
    --tags=http-server,https-server \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --service-account=my-service-account@my-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--zone` | Zone that has RTX A6000 GPUs available. |
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM profile. |
| `--image-family` + `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | Disk capacity & performance. |
| `--accelerator` | Attach one RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `--maintenance-policy=MIGRATE` | VM can be live‑migrated during maintenance. |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restarts if the instance crashes. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional script to run at boot. |
| `--tags` | Enables HTTP/HTTPS firewall rules. |
| `--scopes` | Grants full Cloud Platform access. |
| `--service-account` | Service account to use (replace with your own). |

> **Tip:**  
> *If you don’t have a service account yet, create one via IAM → Service Accounts.*  
> *Make sure the account has the “Compute Admin” role.*

---

## 2️⃣ REST API Request (JSON)

If you prefer to use the REST API directly (or via Terraform, Pulumi, etc.), here’s the exact payload you’d POST to `https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances`.

```json
{
  "name": "my-rtx-a6000",
  "machineType": "projects/my-project/zones/us-central1-b/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 50,
        "diskType": "projects/my-project/zones/us-central1-b/diskTypes/pd-balanced"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-project/zones/us-central1-b/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "MIGRATE",
    "automaticRestart": true
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "my-service-account@my-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update && apt-get install -y python3-pip"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Replace:

* `{PROJECT_ID}` → your GCP project ID (`my-project`).  
* `us-central1-b` → any zone that offers RTX A6000 GPUs.  
* `my-service-account@my-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com` → your own service account.

Send this JSON with an authenticated OAuth token (`Bearer <token>`). You can obtain the token via `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token` or through your preferred SDK.

---

## 3️⃣ Quick Checklist Before Running

| ✅ | Item |
|---|------|
| 1 | Verify that the selected zone (`us-central1-b`, `us-east1-c`, etc.) currently supports RTX A6000 GPUs. |
| 2 | Ensure you have enough quota for GPUs in that region. |
| 3 | Confirm that your billing account is active. |
| 4 | Make sure the service account has the necessary IAM roles (`roles/compute.admin`, `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser`). |
| 5 | If you’re using the REST API, set the correct `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. |

---

### Final Note

Once the instance is running, you’ll see it listed under **Compute Engine → VM Instances**. From there you can SSH into it, install CUDA drivers, and start your workloads. Happy computing!
